subject.title: fix(agents): drop stale internal orphan prompts

question: Should maintainers accept this PR's stale-internal-drop strategy, prefer the preserve-as-context strategy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90759, or pause both until one canonical session-repair contract is chosen?
rationale: Both open PRs address the same session-state bug with different model-visible prompt semantics, and this external PR still lacks real embedded-agent proof, so automation cannot safely decide the product/runtime contract.

options.title: Require proof before this strategy lands
options.body: Keep this PR blocked until redacted embedded-agent logs or terminal output prove the six-source drop behavior and `sessions_send` preservation, then decide whether this is the canonical strategy.

options.title: Prefer the broader proven candidate
options.body: Route maintainers toward https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90759 if preserve-as-context semantics are the desired contract for the canonical issue.

options.title: Pause both strategies
options.body: Ask for a maintainer-authored design decision if neither drop semantics nor preserve-as-context semantics is clearly acceptable yet.

recommendation.title: Require proof before this strategy lands
recommendation.body: Keep this PR blocked until redacted embedded-agent logs or terminal output prove the six-source drop behavior and `sessions_send` preservation, then decide whether this is the canonical strategy.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is closest to the queued-user prompt preservation invariant introduced in PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65478.
